Every Calderwick Scholar studies at the.why: Made up: "Calderwick" does not occur on Wikipedia and names no documented thing, so nothing recorded says anything about it. It is a scholarship under the real class of postgraduate scholarships (a university or a trust could fund one that nobody has written about), and no real rule is contradicted because the real class keeps its own value.

It follows only from the inserted rule applied to the stated membership.

notes: TBox expansion, paired with people-replace-0005. Keeps the revision's relation (educated_in) and new conclusion (study at the University of Cambridge) and gives it to a made-up scholarship, the Calderwick Scholarship, under the real class of postgraduate scholarships, so no old value is pushed out. The derived queries name invented scholars with the scholarship stated in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops, bridge in the prompt): the inserted rule is their only route to Cambridge. The near unrelated query asks about the real Rhodes Scholarship, whose host university is Oxford and must not move to Cambridge; a method that learned a bare 'scholar studies at Cambridge' mapping would leak there. Scholarship and scholar names are invented; the counting step records that they are absent from the corpus. Side facts and checks are those of the paired revision.
